sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Breaking the story down before the agents do
sections.para: Ole Reissmann's diagnosis, agents reading journalism as fragments, and his answer, the newsroom's own breakdown as structured data, match how this newsroom was built: every article ships with a twin, a graph and section summaries, and claims are traced. SPIEGEL is ahead on the allegation as a field.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven lines from his session to our proposal
sections.para: His diagnosis and answer are right; this newsroom ships the breakdown with every article; the counts; claims with ids; the allegation field we should add; and the layers plugged into one pipeline.

sections.label: The problem, in his words
sections.para: Agents fire off queries, grab fragments and stitch a confident summary that can miss what matters, and the publisher has no say. The answer is to publish the structure the article already has, next to it.

sections.label: His answer: do the breakdown first
sections.line: His answer: do the breakdown first
sections.para: SPIEGEL's workflow pulls out actors and events, traces sources and claims, flags allegations the affected party should answer, and was tested for summaries with no human in the loop: newsroom judgement first, sources first-class, the right of reply built in.

sections.label: What this newsroom already ships
sections.para: Every article has a markdown twin, a knowledge graph with verbatim-checked quotes, a one-line and one-paragraph summary of every section, and its sources; the site adds llms.txt, a search index and a reader API. 327 graphs, 3,676 nodes, 819 quotes, 3,674 sections.

sections.label: Actors, events, sources and claims
sections.para: The book's claims register gives every number an id and a rerun command; sources and shadows records every reference's licence, access and quotes; the wire as a graph makes every name a link and every sentence a typed claim.

sections.label: The allegation and the right to respond
sections.line: The allegation and the right to respond
sections.para: We put the other side's answer next to an allegation, and propose signed positions from experts and sources, but the graph has no allegation kind yet: a claim about a party, with whether it was put to them and their answer. That is what to add, aligned with SPIEGEL.

sections.label: Plugging the layers together
sections.para: The layers drift when separate teams own them; here the article, graph, summaries and sources are written by one agent and released as one commit. On MCP, our reader API is a start, and worth comparing notes.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: SPIEGEL's workflow is known only from the post; counts are from 30 October; summaries and graphs are checked for form, not judgement; the allegation field is a proposal.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: Ole Reissmann's post, shared as screenshots, and this site's graphs, summaries, llms.txt, reader API and the book's claims register.
